bevry.description: A web app for cocktail enthusiasts to discover, share, rate, and manage drinks.

project.title: The Project
text: Bevry is a web app created during my master's studies together with four fellow students. The application is aimed at cocktail enthusiasts who enjoy trying new drink creations and sharing their own recipes.
Initially, we focused on the basic functions: viewing, posting, liking, and rating cocktail recipes.

features.title: Features
text: In the second semester of the master's program, we gave the app a new design and added numerous new features to further improve the user experience.

With the new bar inventory feature, users can always keep track of their existing ingredients. Additionally, recommendations based on the ingredients available in the bar stock were integrated. The shopping list simplifies shopping by allowing missing ingredients to be added directly from the recipe. Users can now also create their own ingredients and add substitute ingredients to make recipes even more personalized.
For entertainment at parties, our two new mini-games come into play. One is the turn-based multiplayer game 'Spin the Wheel', and the other is the single-player game 'Mix it Up'.

branding.title: Branding
text: In the course 'Brand Identity & Corporate Design', the corporate identity of Bevry was developed. We worked with Adobe InDesign, Adobe Photoshop, and Figma.
I created the logo, various business stationery, stickers, website designs, and mockups.
Take a look at the brand book!

implementation.title: Implementation
text: The five of us worked with Scrum to organize ourselves. Sprint planning and sprint reviews took place every two weeks during our weekly meetings. We used Jira to create tickets and track their status on the Kanban board.

We also collaborated with fellow students from other master's programs, including 'Photography' for cocktail, marketing, and portfolio photos, 'Graphic Design' for app design and icons, 'Sound Design' for soundtracks and sound effects for the mini-games, and 'Animation' for a loading animation as well as animations within the mini-games.

myTasks.title: My Tasks
text: My main responsibility was in backend development with NestJS. Endpoint documentation was done using OpenAPI in Swagger. In the backend, I was responsible for the implementation of recipes, ingredients, substitute ingredients, as well as the shopping list and bar inventory. I also handled user data management and the implementation of email verification.
Additionally, I was involved in frontend development with Vue.js. I assisted in implementing the new screen designs and integrated both the self-designed icons and the loading animation.

erika.description: An app as a digital companion for climate-friendly actions and regional activities.

project.title: The Project
text: In the second semester of my master's program, I had the opportunity to work on a research project affiliated with the program's research institute. I chose the ERIKA project. The goal of the project is to develop the ERIKA app, which serves as a digital companion for climate-conscious actions in everyday life.

The app aims to promote climate-friendly behavior and highlight regional activities in the Waidhofen a/d Ybbs area. The focus is not only on sustainable content but also on sustainable aspects in the development and design of the app, ensuring a holistic implementation of the concept of sustainability.

implementation.title: The Implementation
text: During my work on the ERIKA research project, I conducted extensive research on the factors crucial for developing a sustainable website.

Additionally, I participated in researching and formulating research questions related to climate-friendly actions in daily life, the impacts of various measures, the role of digitalization, and the application of gamification to support sustainable behavior.
I analyzed and processed survey results and created a clickable prototype of the app.

sustainability.title: Sustainable Web & App Design
text: In all areas of life, we strive for sustainability, but the environmental impact of the internet is often overlooked. The carbon emissions of the internet are equivalent to those of the aviation industry, accounting for about 2% of global emissions.

In my research on sustainable web, app, and email design, I discovered many aspects that contribute to sustainability. These include green hosting, SEO, design, UX, and performance optimization. For instance, choosing colors and fonts, writing efficient code, minimizing HTTP requests, optimizing images, and reducing third-party integrations can help lower the CO₂ footprint.

Sustainable web design is not only ecologically beneficial but also improves user experience, search engine ranking, and accessibility, particularly in regions with limited internet access. Websites that consume fewer resources load faster and offer better performance, enhancing user satisfaction and increasing reach.
I summarized the results of my research in a blog post.

prototyping.title: Prototyping
text: Additionally, I created a Figma prototype for a user story of the ERIKA service. This click dummy visualizes how the service can be used in everyday life to inform users about current sustainable initiatives.

The prototype includes a form through which users can submit their own initiatives. After review and approval, these initiatives appear in the calendar and map views. This allows users not only to participate in events but also to contribute their own ideas to increase their ecological handprint.

In the calendar and map views, users can see all upcoming initiatives and events, such as the weekly market or an upcoming flea market. Each event features a detailed view with a description and information about dates and locations. When GPS is enabled, users receive notifications when they are near an event.

ecocalypse.description: Creation of an immersive video game scene in Unity focusing on worldbuilding and visual storytelling.

project.title: The Project
text: In the second semester of the master’s program, we had the opportunity to participate in one-week workshops on various topics as part of the Summer School. I chose a workshop on 'Environmental Storytelling,' which covered topics like worldbuilding as well as environmental and visual storytelling.

The project involved creating a static or interactive immersive video game scene using Unity and pre-made assets. The scene was meant to depict a realistic game environment that was both visually appealing and functional for a video game setting. Particular emphasis was placed on accurately applying the principles of environmental storytelling learned during the workshop.

In this workshop, we worked in small groups to develop the concept for 'Ecocalypse,' a game in which players inhabit a world devastated by a climate catastrophe. The year is 2035. Just one year ago, a disaster occurred that changed everything: within days, the entire rainforest burned down. The result was a collapse of the global climate, which in turn brought down the world order.

implementation.title: The Implementation
text: For the implementation of the project, I took on several tasks, including worldbuilding, storytelling, and placing objects in the room, such as the newspaper articles. Additionally, I was responsible for selecting the necessary low-poly assets for Unity.

When creating the storyline, we paid special attention to integrating behavioral traces, identity claims, and mood modifiers. These elements had to be cohesive to create an immersive experience. Any inconsistencies in the room, lighting, or sound could break the players’ immersion and disrupt the experience.

scene.title: The Scene
text: The scene is set in a room of an elegant house that was once Joseph’s office. After the unexpected collapse of infrastructure, he barricaded himself there, waiting for the right time to escape to the countryside to reunite with his family.

The player discovers traces of his daily life and preparations for escape, including personal belongings, notes, and supplies. The room is ransacked and bears the marks of a violent raid in which Joseph was killed for his resources. Now, the intruders are using his supplies, while the room paints a vivid picture of Joseph’s desperate struggle for survival and his tragic demise.

objects.title: The Objects
text: Various objects were carefully placed in the room to tell his story and convey the game’s backstory.

The walls feature several newspaper articles that provide information about the crisis and global events. A family portrait shows Joseph’s family and hints at a safe haven in the countryside. A city map with a marked escape route illustrates Joseph’s planned journey.

A wall calendar reveals that the game takes place in January 2035 and that Joseph tried to keep track of time. His detailed daily routine sheds light on how he structured his days to avoid losing his sanity in isolation. On the desk, there is an unfinished letter to Julia, offering insight into Joseph’s thoughts and emotions. Lastly, an advertisement for 'H2-NO' underscores the extreme circumstances of this world, where water has become the most valuable resource.

These objects provide valuable clues about Joseph’s life and the circumstances leading to his current situation. Through this careful planning and execution, we were able to create an immersive and consistent game scene that effectively utilizes the principles of environmental storytelling.

veganAdvent.description: A digital advent calendar with valuable tips and information for a vegan lifestyle.

project.title: The Project
text: The idea behind this advent calendar was to present new information or helpful tips about veganism each day in December. I intentionally chose not to include a feature that checks the current day, ensuring that the website's content is always accessible as part of the 'Print to Mobile' project for my master's program at FH St. Pölten. My goal was not only to share recipes but also to raise awareness of the benefits of a vegan lifestyle.
Additionally, there is a poster with 24 numbered QR codes. Each day in December, users can scan the QR code for the respective day to access the corresponding advent door.

implementation.title: The Implementation
text: I developed the web application using React and Tailwind CSS. The interactive bar chart in door 2 was created with ApexCharts.
On the website, users can switch between Light Mode, Dark Mode, and the system’s default display mode. The colors of the SVG on the homepage also adapt to the selected mode.
More information about the project and the commented source code for my implemented components can be found on GitHub.

trilum.description: Analysis and redesign of the user interface for the wireless Pick-by-Light system TRILUM to enhance usability.

project.title: The Project
text: As part of my bachelor's thesis, I analyzed and redesigned the graphical user interface of the Pick-by-Light system TRILUM. The system, developed by the Fraunhofer Society at the Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits (IIS), served as the foundation for my work.

In collaboration with Fraunhofer IIS, where I was hired as a student assistant in the Supply Chain Services group in Nuremberg following my mandatory internship, I had the opportunity to write my bachelor's thesis. My goal was to improve the usability of the web application.
Access to my bachelor's thesis is password-protected — just reach out to me for the login details

init.title: Starting Point
text: TRILUM is a wireless Pick-by-Light system for warehouse picking and assembly processes. The system guides employees who need to retrieve materials from shelves to the correct compartment using light signals.
However, the focus of my work was on the desktop application developed using the Angular framework. This application is used to coordinate orders, manage inventory, and oversee employees.

implementation.title: Implementation
text: To emphasize user-centricity, the user-centered design process according to ISO standard 9241/210 was applied.
First, the application was analyzed. During this phase, other Pick-by-Light systems were reviewed, and user requirements were documented.

To design and conduct usability tests, appropriate usability evaluation methods were selected. Users were surveyed using a questionnaire, and the think-aloud method was employed to observe user behavior.

Based on the test evaluations, usability issues were identified, and design solutions were developed to improve the user experience. The optimization proposals were then prioritized and implemented in the existing system, followed by a second round of usability testing.

result.title: The Result
text: The results of the follow-up tests show that the system's usability was significantly improved, allowing for more intuitive interaction. Participants not only found the tasks easier to complete but also rated the interaction principles much higher.
